chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad and Muhammad ibn al-Husayn together, from Muhammad ibn Isma'il ibn Bazi', from Mansur ibn Yunus, from Abu al-Jarud, from Abu Ja'far عليه السلام, who said:
I heard Abu Ja'far عليه السلام saying: Allah, Mighty and Majestic, obligated five things upon the servants. They took four and left one. I said: Can you name them for me? May I be sacrificed for you.

He said: Salat, and the people did not know how they should pray, so Jibra'il عليه السلام descended and said: O Muhammad, inform them of the times of their salat. Then zakat was revealed, and he said: O Muhammad, inform them regarding their zakat as you informed them regarding their salat. Then sawm was revealed, and the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله used, when it was the day of 'Ashura', to send to the surrounding villages, and they would fast that day. Then the month of Ramadan was revealed between Sha'ban and Shawwal. Then hajj was revealed, so Jibra'il عليه السلام descended and said: Inform them regarding their hajj as you informed them regarding their salat, zakat, and sawm.

Then wilayah was revealed, and that came to him on the day of الجمعة at 'Arafah. Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed: This day I have perfected for you your religion and completed My favor upon you. The completion of the religion was through the wilayah of 'Ali ibn Abi Talib عليه السلام.

At that, the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله said: My community is newly removed from جاهلية, and whenever I inform them of this concerning my cousin, one speaker will say this and another speaker will say that. So I said within myself, without my tongue speaking it, then a decisive command came to me from Allah, Mighty and Majestic, absolutely, threatening me that if I did not convey it, He would punish me. Then it was revealed: O Messenger, convey what has been sent down to you from your Lord; and if you do not, then you have not conveyed His message. And Allah will protect you from the people. Indeed Allah does not guide the disbelieving people.

So the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله took the hand of 'Ali عليه السلام and said: O people, there was not a Prophet among the Prophets before me except that Allah gave him life, then called him, and he answered Him. So soon I shall be called and I shall answer. I am to be questioned, and you are to be questioned, so what will you say? They said: We bear witness that you have conveyed, advised sincerely, and fulfilled what was upon you. So may Allah reward you with the best reward of the Messengers. He said: O Allah, bear witness—three times. Then he said: O assembly of the Muslims, this is your wali after me, so let the one present among you convey to the absent.

Abu Ja'far عليه السلام said: By Allah, 'Ali عليه السلام was the trustee of Allah over His creation, His unseen, and His religion which He approved for Himself. Then when that which comes came to the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله, he called 'Ali and said: O 'Ali, I wish to entrust you with what Allah entrusted me with, from His unseen, His knowledge, His creation, and His religion which He approved for Himself. By Allah, O Ziyad, he did not associate in it anyone from creation.

Then when that which comes came to 'Ali عليه السلام, he called his children, and they were twelve males, and said to them: O my sons, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has refused except to place in me a sunnah from Ya'qub. Ya'qub called his sons, and they were twelve males, and informed them of their leader. Indeed, I am informing you of your leader. Indeed, these two are the sons of the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله, al-Hasan and al-Husayn عليهما السلام, so listen to them both, obey them both, and support them both. For I have entrusted them with what the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله entrusted me with, from what Allah entrusted him with from His creation, His unseen, and His religion which He approved for Himself.

So Allah made obligatory for them both from 'Ali عليه السلام what He made obligatory for 'Ali عليه السلام from the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله. Neither of them had superiority over the other except by elderness, and al-Husayn would, when al-Hasan was present, not speak in that gathering until he rose.

Then when that which comes came to al-Hasan عليه السلام, he handed that over to al-Husayn عليه السلام. Then when that which comes came to Husayn, he called his elder daughter Fatimah bint al-Husayn عليها السلام and handed to her a wrapped book and an outward will. 'Ali ibn al-Husayn عليه السلام was suffering from illness of the belly, and they thought it was due to his condition, so Fatimah handed the book to 'Ali ibn al-Husayn. Then, by Allah, that book came to us.

Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Jumhur, from Muhammad ibn Isma'il ibn Bazi', from Mansur ibn Yunus, from Abu al-Jarud, from Abu Ja'far عليه السلام, similarly to it.

key_terms.أَمِينُ اللَّهِ: The trustee of Allah over His creation, unseen, and religion.
key_terms.الزَّكَاةُ: The obligatory zakat revealed after salat as a defined religious duty.
key_terms.الصَّلَاةُ: The prescribed salat that was taught with its appointed times.
key_terms.الصَّوْمُ: The prescribed fasting, culminating in the fasting of the month of Ramadan.
key_terms.الْحَجُّ: The pilgrimage whose rites were taught by divine instruction.
key_terms.الْوَلَايَةُ: The divinely mandated authority and guardianship presented as completing the religion.
key_terms.غَيْبِهِ: Allah's unseen, entrusted in this narration to the divinely appointed authority.
key_terms.كِتَابًا مَلْفُوفًا: A wrapped book handed on as part of the transmitted trust and legacy.

ai.seo_question: How does this hadith describe the five obligations of religion and the role of wilayah in completing the faith?
ai.summary: This hadith states that Allah obligated five foundational matters upon the servants, culminating in wilayah, which the narration presents as the perfection and completion of the religion through the wilayah of Imam 'Ali عليه السلام. It also describes the Prophet's صلى الله عليه وآله public proclamation, the transmission of divine trust to Imam 'Ali عليه السلام, and the succession of that trust through the Imams عليهم السلام.
